input.reasoning_summary:
The claim asserts that "Walmart's growing advertising business is the main reason its operating income grew faster than its sales in fiscal 2026."

The claim contains a fundamental factual error: operating income did NOT grow faster than sales in fiscal 2026. The evidence clearly shows:
- Net sales grew 4.7% (from $674,538M to $706,413M)
- Operating income grew only 1.6% (from $29,348M to $29,825M)

This was confirmed by both the filing data (E8, E3) and the computed numeric check (E12), which shows operating income YoY growth of 0.0163 (1.63%), well below the 4.7% sales growth threshold.

Since the core premise of the claim—that operating income grew faster than sales—is factually incorrect, the claim is CONTRADICTED regardless of whether advertising was a driver of any margin improvements.

Additionally, while the filing does mention "growth in higher margin businesses" as a contributor to gross profit improvements (E14, E16), it does not specifically attribute this to advertising as the "main reason" for operating income performance. The filing emphasizes "disciplined inventory management" alongside higher margin businesses, and never singles out advertising as the primary driver.
